title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not a manuscript note. It is page 33 of the typescript of SGA 7 I, Exposé IX (Grothendieck, 'Modèles de Néron et monodromie'). The sheet appears to have been reused as scrap paper: the neighbouring pages carry handwritten notes on graded modules over divided-power polynomial rings, which belong to the 1975–76 cote.

Setting: S is the spectrum of a (strictly) henselian discrete valuation ring with fraction field K and residue field k. ℓ is a prime different from char k. A_K is an abelian variety, U = T_ℓ(A(K̄)) is its ℓ-adic Tate module, and I is the inertia group.

1. End of the remarks after 3.5.1: base change along a morphism of traits S' → S is compatible with condition (iv). Condition (iv) says the inertia acts unipotently on V_ℓ, with (1−σ)^2 = 0 (the Grothendieck criterion). If (iv) holds for A_K, it passes to abelian subschemes and quotients, hence to any isogenous abelian variety, for example the dual A'_K.

2. Corollary 3.5.2. Let g be a topological generator of Z_ℓ(1) = T_ℓ(k̄*). Semi-stable reduction is equivalent to condition (v): I acts on U through its maximal pro-ℓ quotient I(ℓ), which is canonically Z_ℓ(1) by tame ramification theory, and g_U satisfies (1−g_U)^2 = 0. Proof given: a continuous unipotent action of a profinite group on an ℓ-adic vector space has pro-ℓ image, so (v) ⇔ (iv).

3. Theorem 3.6 (semi-stable reduction theorem). Let S be a connected regular noetherian scheme of dimension 1 with function field K, and A_K an abelian variety over K. Then there is a finite Galois extension K'/K such that A_{K'} has semi-stable reduction over the normalization S' of S in K'. This is the central result of the exposé; its proof, on later pages, uses the ℓ-adic criterion together with the finiteness of the image of inertia modulo its unipotent part.
errors: No mathematical errors. The pro-ℓ claim is correct: a unipotent subgroup of GL_n(Z_ℓ), after a lattice choice, lies in a conjugate of the upper unitriangular group, which is pro-ℓ. The identification I(ℓ) ≅ Z_ℓ(1) tacitly needs ℓ ≠ char k and k separably closed (strict henselization), as in the surrounding text.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a typescript page of the published SGA 7 I, Exposé IX (Cor. 3.5.2 and Thm 3.6), apparently recycled as scrap paper. Everything on it is published and correctly credited to Grothendieck.
transcription_corrections: The parenthetical '(I      )' after Z_ℓ(1) is a blank left in the typescript for a cross-reference; it is not missing text to be reconstructed.
'351' is the archive foliation number stamped (and handwritten) on the sheet, not mathematical content.
The page is typed, not handwritten; it belongs to SGA 7 Exp. IX rather than to the divided-power De Rham notes of this cote.
